captions.instagram:
Concept. Not a client project. Larkhill Cooling is a fictional business.

It’s 38 degrees and the AC has died. You find a local air conditioning site, and before you see a phone number, a pop-up asks you to join a newsletter. The number is behind the menu, and nothing says which suburbs they cover.

So we dropped the pop-up, put the suburbs under the headline, added a three-field booking form and kept a call button on screen the whole way down.

Does your site greet people with a pop-up? Free review at prycedigital.com/book

captions.linkedin:
Concept. Not a client project. A fictional air conditioning business, redesigned for the phone.

The old homepage opens with a newsletter pop-up over the whole screen. Close it and the phone number is still three taps away, behind the menu, and nothing says which suburbs they service.

On a hot day, the person on that page wants one thing: someone to come and fix it.

The new version has no pop-up. The suburbs sit under the headline, a three-field form books a visit, and a call button stays on screen the whole way down.

If your trade site leads with a pop-up, I’m happy to take a look: prycedigital.com/book
